problem: Suppose that $f(x)$ is a function such that ${\int }_{3}^{0}\frac{1}{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-1$ and ${\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=6.$ What is the value of ${\int }_{0}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x?$

feedback.worked_solution:
Let's simplify one of the given integrals:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{3}\frac{2}{3}\,g(x)\,\text{d}x & =6 \\ \frac{2}{3}{\int }_{-3}^{3}g(x)\,\text{d}x & =6 \\ {\int }_{-3}^{3}g(x)\,\text{d}x & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Using the adjacent intervals rule and substituting known values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{3}(\frac{5}{2}f(x)-4g(x))\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-3}^{-1}(\frac{5}{2}f(x)-4g(x))\,\text{d}x \\  & \,\,\,+{\int }_{-1}^{3}(\frac{5}{2}f(x)-4g(x))\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

By the sum rule for definite integrals,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{3}(\frac{5}{2}f(x)-4g(x))\,\text{d}x & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x-4{\int }_{-3}^{3}g(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{2}(-4)-4(9) \\  & =-46.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{-1}(\frac{5}{2}f(x)-4g(x))\,\text{d}x & =-46-{\int }_{-1}^{3}(\frac{5}{2}f(x)-4g(x))\,\text{d}x \\  & =-46-(-20) \\  & =-26.\end{aligned}
$$
